newsitem.title: USA: Dollar closes mixed in U.S., cuts overnight losses.
newsitem.headline: Dollar closes mixed in U.S., cuts overnight losses.

text.p: The dollar ended mixed in U.S. trading after paring losses against the yen and scratching out modest gains against the mark, which remained under pressure against the yen, dealers said.
Investors began selling dollars for yen in overnight trade and the dollar's slide continued in New York trading before bargain-hunters emerged to bolster the unit, dealers said.

Players appeared reluctant to hold dollars ahead of the Wednesday release of Japan's Tankan economic report. Some investors feared a strong report would raise the odds of imminent Japanese monetary tightening.

"It would cause a lot of movement in dollar/yen if people thought Japan would raise rates. Then you would see some excitement," said John Hazelton, chief currency dealer at Manufacturers and Traders Bank.
The dollar ended lower on Monday at 107.67/74 yen, down from 107.77/82 at the open, but closed higher at 1.4783/93 marks, up from 1.4772/76.
The yen also rallied against the mark, bolstered by a large buy order from a speculative investor in New York, dealers said.
"One player sold dollars for yen and marks for yen," said Tadatoshi Taso, chief dealer at Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi.
Few observers expect the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates soon, but any surprising strength in the Tankan could stimulate further yen buying, dealers said.
"The Bank of Japan will not move as a result of the Tankan, but if the report is (stronger) than expected, the market may move," Taso said.
Selling of marks against the yen also fueled a smattering of buying of dollars against the mark, and the dollar crawled higher after U.S. trading began.
"The dollar seemed to rebound against the mark. People may have been doing some bargain-hunting," said Jay Wertheimer, senior foreign exchange trader at Banco di Sicilia.

Relatively thin trading may have helped exaggerate the day's price movements, dealers said. A holiday closed markets in London and many U.S. investors and dealers have scheduled vacations this week ahead of next Monday's Labor Day holiday.
"The day was pretty uneventful. We stayed in a range back and forth in New York and there was very little to get excited about," said Hazelton.
Dealers noted the dollar failed to break through technical resistance at 1.48 marks, its high for the session. Key technical support at 107.50 yen held as the day's low.
In other trade the dollar rose to 1.1934/41 Swiss francs from 1.1912/22 at the open. Sterling rose to $1.5573/80 from $1.5565/75.
The dollar edged higher to Canadian $1.3705/10 from C$1.3699/04 at the open. The Australian dollar rose to $0.7910/15 from $0.7906/11.
